runtime_verification.scope: Only the exact operation examples are evidence probes; no oracle, corpus, or frozen contracts were changed.
runtime_verification.summary: Verified getter invocation versus descriptor copy, symbol enumeration, copy of holes/trailing length, isObject classification, nested destination identity, own undefined and inherited validation, fatal-order stop, strict removal of object identity and NaN, shallow selection, __proto__ assignment, and remainder-first partition.

scenarios.setup: Create `{}`, `Object.create(null)`, `[]`, a function, a class instance, `expandable({known:1})`, and a null-prototype record with own `constructor: Object`; also define an enumerable getter on a source object.
operations: Call expandable(source) and inspect its prototype, own keys, property descriptors, and getter counter.
expected_observable_behavior: isObject is true only when typeof is object, non-null, and the observed `.constructor` is exactly Object or Expandable: ordinary object, Expandable, and even the null-prototype record shadowing constructor to Object are true; null-prototype without shadow, array, function, and ordinary class instance are false.

expandable returns a distinct value with Expandable.prototype; Object.assign copies own enumerable string and symbol values, invokes getters, and creates ordinary writable/enumerable/configurable data properties.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Represent constructor/prototype identity separately from structural object contents; an ordinary map test will misclassify instances, null-prototype records, and constructor-shadowed objects.
Represent getter evaluation and descriptor loss in expandable; it is not a descriptor-preserving copy.

scenarios.setup: Create an object with enumerable string keys inserted as `b`, `2`, `a`; an enumerable symbol and a non-enumerable symbol; and a non-enumerable string property.
operations: Call insert({}, source, false), then inspect Reflect.ownKeys and descriptors on destination.
expected_observable_behavior: keys returns Object.keys string keys first in JS order (`2`, `b`, `a`), followed by all own symbols in creation order, including non-enumerable symbols; the non-enumerable string key is excluded.
insert reads and assigns the non-enumerable source symbol too; assignment creates an enumerable own destination symbol. It does not copy the non-enumerable string.
For any falsey input (`undefined`, `null`, `false`, `0`, or empty string), keys returns an empty list without property access.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Property keys must preserve symbol identity and ordering separately from string keys; symbols cannot be stringified for successful merges.
Track enumerability because Object.keys excludes non-enumerable strings while keys explicitly includes even non-enumerable symbols.

scenarios.setup: Build a source with an enumerable getter (incrementing a counter), enumerable non-writable data property, enumerable symbol property, non-enumerable string and symbol properties, nested object, array containing a nested plain object and a class instance value. Define both getter and setter functions on an enumerable accessor descriptor, and give the destination an inherited setter for the same key.
operations: Inspect getter count, Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(copy), nested identity, and copied values.
Merge the accessor source into a destination inheriting a setter; inspect getter/setter counters, stored value, own-property status, and the accessor descriptor on a separate copy.
expected_observable_behavior: The getter counter remains zero: copy reads the own property descriptor and never evaluates the accessor. The enumerable accessor descriptor itself is retained on the copy.
Enumerable own string and symbol descriptors are preserved, including writable/configurable flags; non-enumerable string and symbol properties are omitted.

Nested eligible plain/Expandable objects are recursively copied; arrays are recursively rebuilt with insert, while class instances/functions and other ineligible values retain identity. The result root is `{}` unless source.constructor is exactly Expandable.
Array index holes between present elements survive by index assignment, but trailing hole length is lost: an array of length 4 with only index 0 present copies to length 1.

copy preserves both getter and setter function identities in the enumerable accessor descriptor without invoking either. insert reads the source getter and assignment invokes an inherited destination setter; that assignment need not create an own property.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Preserve accessor getter/setter identity and descriptor flags without evaluation during copy.
Represent sparse array length and holes explicitly; insertion-based cloning collapses trailing holes.
Distinguish plain objects, Expandable, arrays, functions and class instances so recursive copy follows isObject rather than generic map traversal.

scenarios.setup: Create an array `a` and a non-array object value `v`.
expected_observable_behavior: makeArray(a) returns the exact same array object. makeArray(v) returns a new one-element array whose element is exactly v.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Preserve object identity for arrays and wrapped values; avoid always allocating a normalized array.

scenarios.setup: For each destination kind (plain object, Expandable, null-prototype object, class instance and function), set `slot` to a nested object `{base:1}`. Merge `{slot:{added:2}, unknown:4}` with warnings disabled. Also merge a plain-looking record whose own `constructor` is shadowed to Object, and one whose constructor is shadowed to a nonstandard class.
operations: Call insert(destination, source, false), retaining references to each destination slot.
Repeat with warn=true for unknown keys and with an Expandable destination.
expected_observable_behavior: Because source `slot` is an eligible object and each slot destination is an object, insert recursively mutates the existing slot in place for all five destination kinds; `base` remains and `added` appears.

With warnings enabled, arbitrary unknown names are accepted without warning only when `dst.constructor === Expandable`; plain/null-prototype/instance/function destinations treat unknown names as invalid.

Source eligibility is based on `sval.constructor`: an instance shadowing constructor to Object is recursively copied/merged as a plain object; an ordinary object shadowing constructor away from Object is assigned as an ineligible value (identity retained if assignment path applies).
If destination value is null or scalar, eligible source object is deep-copied into it. If destination value is a function, nested object merge is allowed because the destination can have properties.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Model destination object/function mutability independently from source-object eligibility.
Preserve in-place nested object identity when recursively merging.
Represent `.constructor` lookup including own shadowing and prototype inheritance; do not infer kind only from value shape.

scenarios.setup: Use a plain defaults object `{known:1, ownUndefined:undefined}`; an object inheriting `known:1`; and an Expandable destination. Set OPTIONS.invalidOption first to `warn`, then `fatal`; provide sources with ordered keys `unknownFirst`, `known`, `later`.
operations: Call userOptions for own-undefined and inherited-known destinations while capturing warnings.
Call defaultOptions with a new key.
Set OPTIONS.invalidOption=`fatal`; call userOptions with unknownFirst before known/later, then inspect destination after catching the exception; restore global mode.
expected_observable_behavior: Validation tests `dst[key] === undefined`, not own-property existence: an own key whose value is undefined is invalid and warns/skips; a known inherited non-undefined key is accepted and assignment creates/updates an own property.
Expandable destinations accept arbitrary names. defaultOptions uses warn=false and accepts new defaults silently.

In fatal mode OPTIONS.optionError throws Error with `Invalid option "unknownFirst" (no default value).`; iteration stops immediately, so later source keys are not processed. OPTIONS.invalidOption and OPTIONS.optionError are mutable live globals.

source_evidence.method: insert validity check and callback order

unresolved_native_representation_needs: Preserve source enumeration order and stop-on-throw mutation ordering.
Expose mutable global option policy/callback semantics, including warning text and fatal exception.
Distinguish missing from present-with-undefined while also preserving inherited lookup for validation.

scenarios.setup: Destination `items=[NaN, sharedObject, {id:1}, 1, 2]`; source sentinel record contains REMOVE `[NaN, sharedObject, {id:1}, 1]` and APPEND a sparse array of length 3 with only index 1 equal to 7.
operations: Call insert({items}, source, false), inspect array length, element identity/value, and index presence. Also call copy on arrays with internal and trailing holes.
expected_observable_behavior: The APPEND/REMOVE mode triggers only for the exact allowed sentinel-key shape(s) and array operands. REMOVE occurs first via indexOf strict equality: NaN remains; sharedObject is removed by identity; the distinct `{id:1}` remains; numeric 1 is removed.

APPEND uses spread into a new array, so sparse appended holes become explicit undefined entries. Result is `[NaN, {id:1}, 2, undefined, 7, undefined]`, with length 6 and no holes in appended positions.
A hole between defined source array indexes survives copy; trailing holes are lost when copy reconstructs using insert and does not restore source length.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Implement strict identity comparison (including object identity and NaN behavior) rather than structural equality.
Represent sparse arrays, undefined entries, and array length separately; spread materializes holes while index-wise copying can retain internal holes.
Preserve the exact sentinel object shape and key-count check; APPEND/REMOVE are string-key constants.

scenarios.setup: Start with destination `{nested:{a:0}, sequence:[]}` and two definitions that update nested values and append/replace arrays. Also pass a destination object to defaultOptions and userOptions.
operations: Call defaultOptions(dst, def1, def2), then userOptions(dst, user1, user2). Record each return and destination reference.
expected_observable_behavior: Both functions mutate and return the exact destination object. Definitions are applied sequentially in argument order; later scalar values overwrite earlier ones.
defaultOptions delegates with warn=false, userOptions with warn=true; nested merge and array replacement/APPEND/REMOVE behavior is exactly insert.

source_evidence.method: ParseOptions constructor merges options then package defaults

unresolved_native_representation_needs: Preserve shared destination identity and observable mutation between ordered definitions.
Keep default and user merge policy distinct even though both delegate to insert.

scenarios.setup: Options has own nested object, own undefined value, an inherited value, and an own enumerable getter; key-source has enumerable string keys plus a symbol. Also create a null-prototype source with own `__proto__` data key.
operations: Call selectOptions(options, ...keys) and selectOptionsFromKeys(options, keySource). Inspect getter counts, output prototype, own keys and reference identities.
expected_observable_behavior: selectOptions selects own properties only, includes own undefined, excludes inherited keys, and copies values shallowly; nested object reference is shared. Reading an own getter invokes it.
selectOptionsFromKeys uses Object.keys(keySource), so key-source symbol keys are ignored.
Both create `{}` and assign with `subset[key] = value`; selecting an own `__proto__` key changes the result prototype instead of creating an own data property.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Keep selection shallow and own-key-based, distinct from deep copy.
Represent assignment semantics for the special `__proto__` string key (or explicitly model the target behavior); a safe dictionary changes upstream semantics.
Getter side effects occur on direct property reads.

scenarios.setup: Options `{a:1,b:2,c:3,d:4}`; selectors: first has inherited `a` with non-undefined value and own `b:undefined`, second has own `c:null`, and a final empty selector.
operations: Call separateOptions(options, selector1, selector2, selector3); compare options before/after and result order.
expected_observable_behavior: Partitions enumerable own string keys of options in selector order; a selector matches when selector[key] !== undefined, including inherited values and null. Explicit undefined is treated as missing and remains eligible for later selectors/remainder.

Returns the final remainder FIRST, then each selector’s set in argument order: `[ {b:2,d:4}, {a:1}, {c:3}, {} ]`. Does not mutate original options. Selector property getters are evaluated by ordinary lookup.
Active TeX construction destructures `[rest, tex, find]`; common output construction destructures `[jaxOptions, fontOptions]`, proving remainder-first is production behavior.

source_evidence.method: CommonOutputJax separates Jax and font options

unresolved_native_representation_needs: Preserve exact result ordering (remainder-first), selector order, and non-mutating partition.
Model selector property access with prototype inheritance and undefined semantics rather than own-key membership.
Handle special property-name assignment semantics on output option dictionaries.

scenarios.setup: Create one object with inherited `key:1`, another with own `key:undefined`, and another with an own getter for key.
operations: Call lookup(key, object, fallback) for each and lookup on own getter while counting calls.
expected_observable_behavior: Inherited key is ignored and returns fallback; own undefined returns undefined rather than fallback; own getter is invoked and its value returned. With no third argument, fallback is null.
unresolved_native_representation_needs: Preserve own-vs-inherited distinction and own-undefined behavior; do not collapse undefined into missing.
Allow accessor evaluation on lookup and preserve fallback identity/value.

remaining_gaps: Primitive/null top-level inputs, cyclic object graphs, cross-realm constructors, proxies, and throwing accessors/setters remain pending probes and contract decisions; they are not approved exclusions.
This proposal does not exhaust every APPEND/REMOVE malformed sentinel shape or all combinations of source/destination descriptors; these cases remain pending root scope/acceptance review.
No proposed scenario changes the production profile or defines native representation; root must freeze representation and acceptance scope.

type_aliases.semantics: TypeScript is only a type alias for arbitrary string-keyed values (`any`); runtime inputs may also carry symbols, accessors, prototype chains, arrays, functions, and class instances.

supporting_documents_context: Observed before P4/P5 numeric acceptance; historical document fingerprints, not current source invariants
